_doc: 3/8-16 UNC: a unified inch thread and what hangs off it, for heavy inch frames and tripods. Holes (ASME B18.2.8), the socket cap, button and flat countersunk heads (ASME B18.3), the hex cap screw (ASME B18.2.1), nuts, washer, set screw and strength are from the standards as tabulated on the pages each source names; the lock nut and the lengths sold are from distributors' lists and say so. Values are in millimetres, and each rule's text gives the inch figure it was converted from (1 in = 25.4 mm). Its pilot in plastic is an estimate where no figure is published, to measure before trusting. kind as in x1c.json.

proof_stress.rule: Proof stress of an alloy steel socket head cap screw up to 1/2 in: 140 ksi (tensile strength 180 ksi at least). Inch socket screws carry no property class number: ASTM A574 has this one grade

stainless_class.rule: The stainless figure is for alloy group 1 (18-8: 302, 303, 304, 305), cold worked, condition CW. The pages read do not say which condition stock screws are supplied in
stainless_class.source: ASTM F837 (stainless steel socket head cap screws), as tabulated at https://torqbolt.com/astm-f837-f837m-stainless-steel-screws-specifications-suppliers-manufacturers and https://www.boltport.com.ferrobend.com/specifications/astm-f837

stainless_proof_stress.rule: Yield strength (0.2 % offset) of an 18-8 stainless socket head cap screw, cold worked: 40 ksi at least (tensile strength 80 ksi at least)
stainless_proof_stress.source: ASTM F837 (stainless steel socket head cap screws), as tabulated at https://torqbolt.com/astm-f837-f837m-stainless-steel-screws-specifications-suppliers-manufacturers and https://www.boltport.com.ferrobend.com/specifications/astm-f837

pilot.rule: Hole to draw for a 3/8-16 UNC machine screw to form its own thread in printed plastic: 0.343 in. No published figure was found for this size: this is the thread's pitch diameter and 0.2 mm, the margin Bambu Lab's M3 and M4 figures have over theirs, since its guide says the printed hole should come out a little under the pitch diameter. Bambu Lab's guide stops at M4: for a thread this size an insert or a nut is the surer choice. Measure it on your printer before trusting it
pilot.source: Worked out from Bambu Lab (MakerWorld official account), How to design screw holes for 3D printing, https://forum.bambulab.com/t/how-to-design-screw-holes-for-3d-printing/217352; pitch diameter by ASME B1.1 (major diameter less 0.6495 of the pitch)
